source:
# Port of lib/pubid/iho/parser.rb — IHO identifiers: letter series
# (S/P/M/B/C), a number with an optional suffix, and the full component
# tail (edition, supplement, part, annex, appendix + subnumber, volume,
# issue, year qualifier).
#
# == Component model (owner rulings, 2026-11-03)
#
# Every component below is a first-class semantic component: its own
# named capture, its own typed binding, independently addressable in
# the model, URN-encodable and matchable — never a regex/string suffix.
#
#   component    face                capture             binding type
#   edition      x.y.z (bare)        edition             string
#   edition      v1 / v5.1 (alias)   edition_shorthand   string (parse-only;
#                                                        the builder pads to
#                                                        x.y.0 — official IHO
#                                                        edition is dotted
#                                                        x.y.z WITHOUT a year)
#   supplement   Sup N (Suppl N)     supplement          string
#   part         Part X / Part S-102 part                string (letter,
#                                                        number, or SERIES
#                                                        REFERENCE)
#   part         -X / -S-102 (short) part                string (hyphenated)
#   annex        Annex A             annex               string
#   appendix     Appendix B          appendix            string
#   appendix     Appendix D-2        appendix_subnumber  string (the -2)
#   volume       Vol. N              volume              string
#   volume       /N (short)          volume              string (the slash
#                                                        chain, P-1/21 or
#                                                        P-5/2020)
#   volume       N (bare, legacy)    volume              string (the yearbook
#                                                        year IS a volume —
#                                                        one serial-locator
#                                                        component)
#   issue        (N) / Issue N       issue               string
#   year         (2024)              year                string (the with-year
#                                                        qualifier on
#                                                        standards; NOT a
#                                                        serial locator)
#
# == Component-edition duality (owner ruling: "this can happen with any
#    independently publishable artifacts")
#
# Supplement, part, annex, appendix and volume can be published on
# their own publication cycle, so EACH carries an optional
# `<kind>_edition` (+ `<kind>_year` qualifier) of its own, mutually
# exclusive with the base edition context:
#
#   within-edition:        IHO P-6 1.0.0 Vol. 2       (the volume rides
#                                                   the base's edition)
#   separately-published:  IHO P-6 Vol. 2 1.0.1       (the volume carries
#                          IHO S-98 Part A 1.0.0       its own edition;
#                          IHO S-158 Part S-102 0.2.0  the base is
#                                                      cited edition-less)
#
# In the URN the ed- segment attaches to the node it follows, so the
# same positional slot records both modes.
#
# The part has a COMPACT face, hyphenated onto the code — `IHO S-5-B`
# (lettered part), `IHO S-100-1` (numbered part), `IHO S-158-S-102`
# (series-reference part) — which both parses and renders; the
# canonical expanded face stays `IHO S-100 x.y.z Part 1`. Gluing a part
# onto the code without a separator (S-5A) is DISALLOWED as a form: it
# cannot extend to numbered parts without ambiguity (S-1001 = series
# 1001 vs series 100 part 1). The four lettered bases the corpus
# records (S-5A, S-5B, S-8A, S-8B) are LEGACY data spellings: they
# still parse as aliases (S-5A == S-5 Part A) but are never rendered;
# the owner rules later whether to reject them outright.
#
# Series-reference parts: a check standard applied to another IHO
# series cites the applied series as its part — `IHO S-158 0.2.0 Part
# S-102` (the wild glued `S-158-102` spelling is a legacy alias whose
# normalization to Part S-102 needs an IHO series table; the syntax
# alone cannot tell it from S-100-1 = Part 1, so it currently parses
# as the plain number part).
#
# Two main syntaxes per the owner ruling: `IHO S-100 1.0.0` (dated =
# edition-specific) and `IHO S-100` (undated = edition-non-specific).
# A year beside an edition is the with-year variant qualifier
# (`IHO S-100 1.0.0 Part X (2024)`), never a year-keyed docidentifier —
# year-keyed docidentifiers for edition-keyed products are wrong. The
# continuously-updated series have ONE serial locator, the volume:
# P-1 and P-6 are volume-keyed (`IHO P-1 Vol. 30 (1)`), and the
# yearbook year IS a volume (`IHO P-5 Vol. 2020`) — the bare year
# (`IHO P-5 2020`) and all year-faced forms are parse-only legacy
# aliases that bind into the volume component, never rendered.
#
# Aliases: "Suppl" (canonical face Sup, the M-2 spelling — why abbreviate
# by two letters when Annex and Appendix stay full-length), "App"/"Ap."
# (canonical face Appendix), the hyphenated compact part face (S-5-B ==
# S-5 Part B, S-100-1 == S-100 Part 1), the legacy glued lettered bases
# (S-5A, parse-only), "S-100 v1..v5.1" (edition shorthand), "Issue N"
# (canonical (N)), the bare year (canonical Vol. N).
#
# == URN segment grammar (positional, containment-ordered)
#
# The URN mirrors the containment tree, one semantic atom per segment:
# Part contains Annexes; Annex contains Appendices; a D-2 subnumber is
# a child atom of Appendix D. No key.value concatenations — every
# non-number component is a marker-prefixed segment whose marker is the
# lowercased human-face token (edition follows ISO's ed- precedent).
# An S-4 specification is a child of its Part (the citation letter rides
# the part- atom), with the dotted sub and the parenthesized variant as
# its own children:
#
#   urn:iho:<type>:<number>[:ed-<x.y.z>][:year-<yyyy>]
#     [:sup-<n>[:ed-<x.y.z>][:year-<yyyy>]]
#     [:part-<X>[:ed-<x.y.z>][:year-<yyyy>]]
#     [:spec-<n>[:specsub-<n>][:specvar-<X>]]
#     [:annex-<A>[...]]
#     [:appendix-<B>[:<sub>][...]]
#     [:vol-<n>[:issue-<n>][...]]
#     [:year-<yyyy>]
#
#   position  segment          value vocabulary            containment
#   --------  ---------------  --------------------------  ------------------
#   1         <type>           s / p / m / b / c           namespace root
#   2         <number>         digits + : suffix; may      document code
#                              span bare segments until
#                              the first marker
#   3         ed-<x.y.z>       dotted a.b.c                edition qualifier;
#   4         year-<yyyy>      19xx/20xx                   ATTACHES TO THE
#                                                      NODE IT FOLLOWS: the
#                                                      base (no component
#                                                      before it) or the
#                                                      component whose
#                                                      segment precedes
#   5         sup-<n>          1*digit                     wraps the base
#   6         part-<X>         letter (case kept),         contains annexes
#                              digits [*letter], or a      and S-4 specs
#                              series reference
#                              [SPMBC]-<digits>
#   7         spec-<n>         [1-6]dd, only under an      child of part (the
#                              S-4 anchor (s:4)            S-4 leaf; the
#                                                          section is the
#                                                          hundreds digit,
#                                                          derivable, never
#                                                          emitted)
#   8         specsub-<n>      1*digit, only after spec-   child of spec
#   9         specvar-<X>      upper letters, after        child of spec
#                              spec- or specsub-
#   10        annex-<A>        upper letter (case kept)    contains appendices
#   11        appendix-<B>     upper letter or digits      contains subnumber
#   12        <sub>            1*digit, BARE, only         child of appendix
#                              directly after appendix-
#   13        vol-<n>          1*digit (incl. yearbook     contains issue
#                              years, Vol. 2020)
#   14        issue-<n>        1*digit, only after vol-    child of volume
#
# The number occupies every leading bare segment up to the first
# marker, so a colon number (S-158:100) round-trips without escaping;
# after the markers the only bare segment allowed is the appendix
# subnumber in its own slot. Both the year qualifier and the volume are
# marker-tagged so neither can collide with a colon-number segment (the
# #637 hazard, kept under the positional scheme). Letters are
# case-preserved: part-A and part-a are distinct documents.
#
# Legacy 2.0.x spellings remain decodable but are never emitted: the
# bare a.b.c segment (edition), the dotted keys part./annex./suppl./
# ap./appendix./vol./issue. and the single-letter y. year tag (whose
# value decodes into the volume — the serial-locator unification).
#
# == S-4 loose-leaf sections and specifications (issue #691; owner
#    rulings of 2026-11-11)
#
# The S-4 loose-leaf publication cites its regulations/specifications as
# <letter>-<hundreds><seq>: B-401 is Part B, Section 400, item 01. ONE
# component, not two tiers: the spec number IS the leaf; the SECTION is
# the hundreds digit, DERIVED (never stored, never emitted). The `00`
# slot (B-400) IS the section-level citation, so "S-4 Part B, Section
# 400" and "IHO S-4 B-400" are one identity, two spellings.
#
#   capture         example            role
#   spec            B-401 -> "401"     the leaf number (3 digits,
#                                      hundreds 1-6: sections 100-600)
#   spec_sub        B-122.1 -> "1"     the dotted sub
#   spec_variant    B-521(I) -> "I"    the parenthesized variant
#   spec_part       B-401 -> "B"       the citation letter (the builder
#                                      binds it into `part`; a Part-rule
#                                      capture must agree)
#   spec_section    ", Section 400" -> "400"  the long form's spelled
#                                      section (becomes `spec` alone;
#                                      checked against a citation)
#
# Faces: canonical compact "IHO S-4 B-401" (dated: "IHO S-4 4.10.0
# B-401"); long "S-4 Part B, Section 400" (a normalizing parse; also
# takes a trailing citation: "S-4 Part B, Section 400, B-401", where the
# spelled section only cross-checks the citation's derived section); bare
# "B-401" (implicit S-4 anchor; B only — bare C-x stays the Circular
# Letter series). The builder binds the anchor: a citation requires the
# S-4 anchor (or synthesizes it for the bare form).
#
# Reserved numbers ("NOT CURRENTLY USED" in the S-4 contents — B-170,
# B-230, B-305, B-323 in Ed 4.9.0 and 4.10.0) parse and resolve AS
# RESERVED, never invalid; the edition-keyed registry lives in the pubid
# gem (data/iho/s4-reserved-specs.yaml).
#
# URN atoms: part-<letter>:spec-<n>[:specsub-<n>][:specvar-<X>] — the
# section is NOT emitted (derivable); the citation letter rides the
# existing part- atom (case preserved: part-B).
#
# Edition 2: ruby#400's capture-flatten keeps text captures over
# reference-built rules as the matched text, so the v2 tree is the v1
# tree plus named leaves for non-captured structure.

grammar PubidIho version "0.3.0" edition 2 {
  digit = %x30-39
  upper = %x41-5A
  lower = %x61-7A
  letter = upper / lower
  space = " "
  dash = "-"
  dot = "."

  series = ("S" / "P" / "M" / "B" / "C") as type
  number_suffix = (":" 1*digit)
  number = (1*digit [number_suffix]) as number
  # The compact part face, hyphenated onto the code: S-5-B (lettered),
  # S-100-1 (numbered) and S-158-S-102 (series reference) — the dash
  # replaces the old bare-glued suffix, so a number like S-1001 stays a
  # whole number (the dash is what makes the part unambiguous). The
  # dash is an inlined literal: a named dash ref here collides with the
  # sequence's own dash node in the edition-2 tree.
  compact_part = "-" ((("S" / "P" / "M" / "B" / "C") dash (1*digit)) / (1*digit [*letter]) / upper) as part
  # LEGACY glued lettered bases (S-5A, S-5B, S-8A, S-8B in the corpus):
  # parse-only aliases, never rendered. Kept because the records exist;
  # the owner rules later whether to reject them.
  glued = upper as part

  # The official edition is the dotted x.y.z; "v1"/"v5.1" is the S-100
  # shorthand (parse-only, the builder pads to x.y.0).
  edition = space (1*digit dot 1*digit dot 1*digit) as edition
  v_edition = space "v" ((1*digit) ["." (1*digit)]) as edition_shorthand
  # The with-year qualifier on standards: a parenthesized year beside an
  # edition. This is the ONLY base-level year capture — periodical
  # years are volumes (the serial-locator unification).
  year_qualifier = space "(" (("19" / "20") 2*digit) as year ")"

  # The series-reference part value: a check standard applied to
  # another IHO series (S-158 checks S-102). Ordered FIRST so "Part
  # S-102" takes the series-reference branch, not the lone letter.
  part_series_ref = (("S" / "P" / "M" / "B" / "C") dash (1*digit))
  part_value = (part_series_ref / (1*digit [*letter]) / upper) as part

  # Component-edition duality: each independently-publishable component
  # may carry its own edition (+ year qualifier), mutually exclusive
  # with the base edition context. The captures are position-scoped
  # (<kind>_edition / <kind>_year) so the model knows which component
  # the edition belongs to and the URN attaches ed- to the node it
  # follows.
  part = space "Part" space part_value [part_dated] [part_section_tail]
  part_dated = {
    part_edition_rule
    [part_year_rule]
  }
  part_edition_rule = space (1*digit dot 1*digit dot 1*digit) as part_edition
  part_year_rule = space "(" (("19" / "20") 2*digit) as part_year ")"

  # --- S-4 loose-leaf sections and specifications (see the header) ---
  # The spec number's vocabulary: the S-4 sections run 100-600 (Part C
  # 100-500), so the leaf number is 3 digits with hundreds digit 1-6 —
  # the same shape the bare citation branch leans on to keep the B
  # Bibliographic series (B-1..B-13 style) distinct from B-4xx specs.
  spec_shape = ("1" / "2" / "3" / "4" / "5" / "6") digit digit
  spec_number = spec_shape as spec
  spec_subnumber = dot (1*digit) as spec_sub
  spec_variant = "(" (1*upper) as spec_variant ")"
  # The citation letter is the spec's part (A/B/C); the builder binds it
  # into `part` and rejects a conflicting Part-rule capture.
  spec_citation_body = ("A" / "B" / "C") as spec_part dash spec_number [spec_subnumber] [spec_variant]
  # The compact anchor form: the citation follows the code after one
  # space ("IHO S-4 B-401").
  spec_citation = space spec_citation_body
  # The spelled section long form: "Part B, Section 400" — the spelled
  # number becomes the spec (the section-level citation), and a trailing
  # citation (", Section 400, B-401") makes it a cross-check only. The
  # commas are inlined literals: named comma refs collide as duplicate
  # edition-2 tree nodes under the entry's alternation (the same node
  # collision the compact_part dash-ref comment documents).
  part_section_tail = {
    "," space "Section" space (spec_shape as spec_section)
    ["," space spec_citation_body]
  }

  # The bare citation branch (the entry's FIRST alternative): "B-401" /
  # "IHO B-401" — implicit S-4 anchor (the builder synthesizes series S
  # number 4). B only: bare C-x stays the Circular Letter series, and the
  # 3-digit [1-6]xx shape keeps the B Bibliographic series (B-12) on the
  # main branch.
  bare_spec_citation = [("IHO" space)] ("B" as spec_part) dash spec_number [spec_subnumber] [spec_variant]

  supplement = space ("Suppl" / "Sup") space (1*digit) as supplement [supplement_dated]
  supplement_dated = {
    supplement_edition_rule
    [supplement_year_rule]
  }
  supplement_edition_rule = space (1*digit dot 1*digit dot 1*digit) as supplement_edition
  supplement_year_rule = space "(" (("19" / "20") 2*digit) as supplement_year ")"

  annex = space "Annex" space upper as annex [annex_dated]
  annex_dated = {
    annex_edition_rule
    [annex_year_rule]
  }
  annex_edition_rule = space (1*digit dot 1*digit dot 1*digit) as annex_edition
  annex_year_rule = space "(" (("19" / "20") 2*digit) as annex_year ")"

  appendix_value = (upper / (1*digit)) as appendix
  appendix_subnumber = dash (1*digit) as appendix_subnumber
  appendix = space ("Appendix" / "App" / "Ap.") space appendix_value [appendix_subnumber] [appendix_dated]
  appendix_dated = {
    appendix_edition_rule
    [appendix_year_rule]
  }
  appendix_edition_rule = space (1*digit dot 1*digit dot 1*digit) as appendix_edition
  appendix_year_rule = space "(" (("19" / "20") 2*digit) as appendix_year ")"

  volume = space "Vol." space (1*digit) as volume [volume_issue]
  volume_issue = (space "Issue" space (1*digit) as issue) / (space "(" (1*digit) as issue ")")
  # The volume's short face — the slash chain ("IHO P-1/21",
  # "IHO P-5/2020"). The slash no longer joins the number.
  volume_short = "/" ((1*digit) as volume) [volume_dated]
  # LEGACY bare year ("IHO P-5 2024"): the yearbook year IS a volume,
  # so a bare year binds INTO the volume component. Parse-only alias;
  # the canonical print is "Vol. N".
  volume_bare_year = space (("19" / "20") 2*digit) as volume
  # The volume's own edition (+ year), shared by the Vol. and slash
  # forms.
  volume_dated = {
    volume_edition_rule
    [volume_year_rule]
  }
  volume_edition_rule = space (1*digit dot 1*digit dot 1*digit) as volume_edition
  volume_year_rule = space "(" (("19" / "20") 2*digit) as volume_year ")"

  # The edition slot accepts the dotted form or the v-shorthand; the
  # with-year qualifier may sit right after it.
  dated = {
    (edition / v_edition)
    [year_qualifier]
  }

  # The serial tail picks exactly one discriminator: the long volume
  # (with its optional issue) or the legacy bare year — both bind the
  # volume component, and both may carry the volume's own edition.
  serial = {
    (volume / volume_bare_year)
    [volume_dated]
  }

  identifier = {
    [("IHO" space)]
    series
    dash
    number
    [compact_part]
    [glued]
    [volume_short]
    [dated]
    [supplement]
    [part]
    [spec_citation]
    [annex]
    [appendix]
    [serial]
    [year_qualifier]
  }

  # The entry dispatches the bare citation branch first (PEG order): a
  # bare "B-401"-shaped input takes the S-4 branch, everything else the
  # main identifier.
  identifier_entry = {
    bare_spec_citation / identifier
  }

  entry identifier: identifier_entry

  test {
    accept "S-5"
    accept "IHO S-5 Appendix 2"
    accept "IHO B-12 3.0.0"
    accept "IHO P-5 2024"
    accept "P-5 2024"
    accept "IHO P-5 Vol. 2024"
    accept "IHO P-5/2024"
    accept "IHO B-7 Vol. 2023"
    accept "IHO P-1 Vol. 30"
    accept "IHO P-1 Vol. 30 (2)"
    accept "IHO P-1 Vol. 30 Issue 2"
    accept "IHO P-1/21"
    accept "IHO P-1/21 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-100 5.0.0 Part 2"
    accept "IHO S-98 1.0.0 Part A"
    accept "IHO S-65 1.1.0 Annex A"
    accept "IHO S-122 1.0.0 Appendix D-2"
    accept "IHO S-52 4.0.0 Appendix 1"
    accept "IHO M-2 Sup 1"
    accept "IHO M-2 Suppl 6"
    accept "IHO S-66 2.0.0 Sup 4"
    accept "IHO S-5-B"
    accept "IHO S-100-1"
    accept "IHO S-100-1 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO P-6-3 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-5A"
    accept "IHO S-5A 1.0.2"
    accept "IHO S-5 1.0.2 Part A"
    accept "IHO S-100 5.0.0 Part 2 (2024)"
    accept "IHO S-100 v5.1"
    accept "IHO S-100 v1"
    accept "IHO S-100 1.0.0 (2024) Part A"
    accept "IHO S-53 Ap. 1 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-98 Part A 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-158:100 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-158:100 Part 2 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-1001"
    accept "IHO S-158 Part S-102 0.2.0"
    accept "IHO S-158-S-102 0.2.0"
    accept "IHO P-6 1.0.0 Vol. 2"
    accept "IHO P-6 Vol. 2 1.0.1"
    accept "IHO S-98 1.0.0 Annex A"
    accept "IHO S-100 5.0.0 Sup 1 2.0.0"
    # --- S-4 loose-leaf sections and specifications ---
    accept "IHO S-4 B-401"
    accept "IHO S-4 4.10.0 B-401"
    accept "IHO S-4 B-122.1"
    accept "IHO S-4 B-521(I)"
    accept "IHO S-4 B-351.1(I)"
    accept "IHO S-4 B-400"
    accept "IHO S-4 B-170"
    accept "B-401"
    accept "IHO B-401"
    accept "B-122.1"
    accept "B-521(I)"
    accept "IHO S-4 Part B, Section 400"
    accept "S-4 Part B, Section 400"
    accept "IHO S-4 Part B, Section 400, B-401"
    accept "B-12"
    reject "IHO S-4 B-4"
    reject "IHO S-4 B-40"
    reject "IHO S-4 B-800"
    reject "nonsense"
    reject "IHO B-12 3.0"
    reject "IHO P-5 1850"
  }

  bindings identifier_entry {
    type -> type (string)
    number -> number (string)
    part -> part (string)
    part_edition -> part_edition (string)
    part_year -> part_year (string)
    annex -> annex (string)
    annex_edition -> annex_edition (string)
    annex_year -> annex_year (string)
    appendix -> appendix (string)
    appendix_subnumber -> appendix_subnumber (string)
    appendix_edition -> appendix_edition (string)
    appendix_year -> appendix_year (string)
    supplement -> supplement (string)
    supplement_edition -> supplement_edition (string)
    supplement_year -> supplement_year (string)
    edition -> edition (string)
    edition_shorthand -> edition_shorthand (string)
    year -> year (string)
    volume -> volume (string)
    volume_edition -> volume_edition (string)
    volume_year -> volume_year (string)
    issue -> issue (string)
    spec -> spec (string)
    spec_sub -> spec_sub (string)
    spec_variant -> spec_variant (string)
    spec_part -> spec_part (string)
    spec_section -> spec_section (string)
  }
}
